Relocation-related land disputes are a conditional risk. Whole-of-islands targets and remote warning approaches describe planned capacity, not verified beneficiaries or effects.

geographic_notes.text: The draft-marked March 2025 NC3 describes historical severe freshwater shortage and well salinity in South Tarawa and Banaba during droughts; it separately mentions temporary abandonment of unspecified islands.
The draft-marked March 2025 NC3 describes water-reserve declarations on private land generating tensions, disputes and vandalism; encroachment is separately noted in South Tarawa, Banaba and Tabakea.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 13 of 13 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No countrywide causal estimate of climate impacts on conflict or violence is established by these sources.
Full subnational coverage and independently evaluated long-term response effectiveness remain gaps.

The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

The 2023–2024 household survey reports national results, not island-level exposure; total affected population differs between its key-results page and detailed text, so no population-wide total is used.
The government NC3 remains visibly draft-marked and gives no scenario or time horizon for relocation-related disputes; current water-reserve conflict is not attributed to climate change.
No accessible primary evidence in this search measured the prevalence of climate-related conflict or the outcomes of whole-of-islands and early-warning interventions.
Compound disaster-impact percentages were excluded because narrative wording and table denominator headings are ambiguous.
The NC3 mentions unspecified islands temporarily abandoned; no abandonment is assigned to South Tarawa or Banaba.
Local land and reserve disputes are not evidence of climate-driven organized violence.
